summary: This bill requires the Secretary of Agriculture to issue and regularly update cybersecurity and digital service regulations for Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards used in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), mandating the use of chip-enabled EBT cards, establishing user interface requirements for states, and prohibiting certain PIN/password requirements, while also providing reimbursement for states and grants for retailers to upgrade to chip-enabled payment terminals.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates states to upgrade EBT cards to chip-enabled technology and requires the Secretary to reimburse states for all reasonable costs associated with this upgrade, including one-time costs, annual fees, and delivery costs. It also establishes a grant program for eligible entities to upgrade payment terminals. These provisions directly lead to increased federal spending to cover these costs.

The bill aims to enhance the security and usability of EBT cards for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) by requiring chip-enabled cards, improved user interfaces, and better fraud reporting and reimbursement mechanisms. It also prohibits replacement fees for cards due to malfunction, fraud, or expiration. These measures are designed to protect and improve access to SNAP benefits for recipients, thereby strengthening the social safety net.

The bill mandates new federal spending through state reimbursements for EBT card upgrades, a grant program for retailers, and administrative costs for implementing cybersecurity regulations. These provisions have no offsetting revenue or cuts, creating minor new outlays incidental to the primary cybersecurity focus.
